data.title: KBRA Assigns AA Rating, Stable Outlook to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, NY Transportation Revenue Refunding Green Bonds, Series 2026A (Climate Bond Certified)
data.description: In New York, credit rating agency KBRA has assigned a long-term rating of AA to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority's NY Transportation Revenue Refunding Green Bonds, Series 2026A (Climate Bond Certified). Additionally, they have affirmed the long-term rating of AA on outstanding Transportation Revenue Bonds, with a Stable Outlook. The rating actions are based on key credit considerations, including the strong coverage of annual debt service provided by the gross revenue pledge.

data.title: LSTA, Inc. Welcomes SEC Proposal Clarifying Treatment of Discretionary Trading Authority Under Custody Rule
data.description: LSTA, Inc. expressed appreciation for the Securities and Exchange Commission's proposed amendments to the investment adviser custody rule. The organization particularly welcomed the exception for authorized discretionary trading activity. This move is seen as a positive step in addressing industry uncertainties. The proposed amendments aim to provide clarity and common-sense solutions to longstanding issues. LSTA, Inc. views this proposal as significant progress in resolving key matters within the industry.

data.title: ComEd, SunVest Celebrate Energization of Near-8 Megawatt DC Community Solar Array at DeKalb Taylor Municipal Airport
data.description: In Chicago, ComEd and SunVest, a local solar developer, held an event to mark the activation of a special community solar project situated at the DeKalb Taylor Municipal Airport. This project, located next to the airfield, benefits the community financially and helps lower power bills for local residents. The array has a nearly eight-megawatt capacity, with 60 percent of the subscriptions set aside for low-to-moderate income (LMI) customers in the DeKalb area.

data.title: Did Gas Vehicle Sales Just Dip Below 50% For The First Time?
data.description: The increasing popularity of electric vehicles is evident in recent sales figures, with reports showing a significant uptick. Despite some discrepancies in the data, there is a clear indication that soaring fuel prices are negatively impacting the demand for gas-powered cars. Speculation suggests that gas vehicle sales may have recently fallen below 50% for the first time, marking a potential shift towards electric vehicles.

data.title: First Solar Sues Corning Subsidiary, Chinese Rival Over Patent Infringement
data.description: On Friday, First Solar saw a 2% increase in its stock following the filing of a lawsuit. The lawsuit was against a Corning subsidiary and a Chinese rival for patent infringement.

data.title: Stock Market Finishes Strong, Yields Off Highs; Micron, Meta, Nvidia, Tesla In Focus: Weekly Review
data.description: The stock market wrapped up with notable highs, as the Nasdaq reached a peak and the S&P 500 bounced back from crucial support levels, amid decreasing Treasury yields from prolonged highs. This positive turn of events in the market was highlighted by key companies such as Micron, Meta, Nvidia, and Tesla. Overall, the market's performance reflected a strong finish, with the Nasdaq hitting a high point and the S&P 500 showcasing resilience. This weekly review emphasizes the successful outcomes in the stock market, with significant focus on the performances of key players like Micron, Meta, Nvidia, and Tesla, contributing to the market's overall positive trend.

data.title: Jobs Report: Soft Hiring Lifts S&P 500, Sinks Rate-Hike Odds; AI Effect?
data.description: The likelihood of an October Federal Reserve rate increase has decreased significantly. Following the release of the Jobs Report, which showed weaker-than-expected hiring numbers, the S&P 500 experienced a boost while the odds of a rate hike decreased. Some analysts are attributing this shift to potential impacts from artificial intelligence.

data.title: Ethereum Layer-2 platform Blast, which was worth $2.3 billion, is closing due to high costs. Users must withdraw assets by Oct. 26.
data.description: The operating costs of a Blast company have now surpassed the revenue being generated by its Ethereum layer-2. As a result, the company has requested users to withdraw their assets to the mainnet before October 26.
